$comment: The database Survey Definitions (GovernanceActionProcess + chained steps) RE's Survey tab
lists and executes for the 'PostgreSQL Database' technology type — the database counterpart
of ../survey-definitions/_batch.json (Slice 12, Phase 1b coordinator brief). A SEPARATE
directory/batch rather than a shared manifest with the repo definitions: bootstrap.py
(BATCH_MANIFEST_FILE) discovers batches one per directory, each with its own canary and its
own post-heal reconciler scripts — the repo batch's reconcile_survey_definition_links.py has
no notion of a database Survey Definition and vice versa, so they cannot share one manifest
even though both live under docs/dr-egeria/.
Runs after questions (see ../_folder_order.json), for the same reason the repo batch does:
each document's 'Link Element To Scope' commands bind the definition to Question terms by
name, and processing this batch while the questions batch is absent succeeds but creates no
ScopedBy link at all — the definition then looks healthy (its own canary present) while the
scoped lookup that depends on those links silently returns nothing.
NOT IDEMPOTENT — see ../survey-definitions/_batch.json's own comment for the full incident
history (2026-08-13, 2026-08-19) behind this rule; the same Dr.Egeria 'Link First/Next
Process Step' non-dedup mechanism applies here unchanged. Only heal this batch when its
canary is MISSING, and always run the reconciler after a heal.
Canary is keyed on qualified_name (author-controlled in the document itself, like the repo
batch's): 'GovActionProcess::DatabaseAnalysisSurvey' is the largest of the three definitions
(4 steps: postgres_column_profile, postgres_nested_columns, db_derived, postgres_operations)
and its process element is created after all of its steps, so its presence means the
document ran to completion. Listed last in `files` for the same reason the repo batch orders
its own canary last, even though these three documents are otherwise independent of each
other (each is fully self-contained — its own process, steps and scope links — so, unlike
the repo batch, file order here is not a real dependency order, just canary-last convention).
Documents here are generated by ../../../scripts/generate_database_survey_definition.py from
../database_survey_types.csv — edit the CSV and regenerate, don't hand-edit the markdown.
Added 2026-09-26 in the SAME change that generated the documents, after
tests/test_reachability_audit.py's TestSurveyDefinitionsAreRestorable caught the three
database documents living in ../survey-definitions/ with no manifest of their own — a heal
would have restored only the repo definitions and left these three silently absent, with the
repo batch's own canary still reporting healthy.

post_heal.reason: Link First/Next Process Step are not idempotent; strip duplicate step edges a heal may have created.

post_heal_checks.reason: Report-only: ScopedBy links vs. each document's own 'Link Element To Scope' blocks. Never writes on this path — a heal must not silently remove or add scope links; it only surfaces drift for a person to act on.
